payload.a_b_finding: (a): the carve-out (test_second_person_inside_a_quotation_is_not_flagged) exists and covers exactly this shape, but the single-quote pairing regex in scripts/verify_episode_observations.py requires a non-letter on both sides of each delimiter; the advisory excerpt's own verbatim word you're has a letter-adjacent apostrophe, which breaks the closing-delimiter lookahead and leaves that quoted span unpaired, so its you was read as unquoted prose. Switching both excerpts from single to double quotes (zero words changed) restores pairing -- verified with triggers_for() returning [] on the reworded statement.

triage_candidates.statement: scripts/verify_episode_observations.py's single-quote span regex fails to pair a legitimately quoted excerpt when the excerpt's own verbatim text contains a letter-adjacent apostrophe (e.g. a contraction like "you're" or a possessive), because the pairing search treats that internal apostrophe as a candidate delimiter and the lookahead/lookbehind guard then fails on both sides. Observed live on launcher-hygiene-002.a3 (LAUNCH_ORDER:lh-episode-rewording). Not fixed here -- the guard and its test file are explicitly out of scope for this run. Recommend: either a house convention of double-quoting any verbatim excerpt containing an apostrophe, or a small regex fix so an internal apostrophe cannot break pairing -- decision belongs to the guard's owner.
